subtitle: Cross-check of 18/Oct/2026, 14th day of the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno): Polymarket at the confirmed reading of 18/Oct, 17:44 BRT, the twenty-one national polls conducted after the vote, including Vox Brasil of 18/Oct, Ipespe/Abrapel and Veritá of 17/Oct and Gerp of 16/Oct, the official [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) final tally and the press flow of 17 and 18/Oct.

candidates.name: Lula
candidates.header: PRICE: 20.50% (cumulative volume USD 26.35M) in the winner contract, confirmed reading of 18/Oct, 17:44 BRT, falls 3.00pp against the confirmed reading of 17/Oct at 16:59 BRT, published in the previous update. BALLOT: 45.16% of the valid votes in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno). POLLS: 46.4% to 44.6% in Vox Brasil of 18/Oct, 51% of the valid votes; 46% to 48% in Ipespe/Abrapel and 48.9% of the valid votes in Veritá of 17/Oct; 45% to 50% in Gerp of 16/Oct.
fortes: He leads both Vox Brasil polls conducted after the vote: 46.4% to 44.6% on 18/Oct, within the 2.15-point margin, with 51% of the valid votes, and 44.2% to 42.7% on 09/Oct.

Between each pollster's previous and current wave, the distance to Flávio Bolsonaro in total votes falls from 5 to 2 points in Ipespe/Abrapel and from 9 to 5 in Gerp, and his lead in Vox Brasil goes from 1.5 to 1.8 points.
🏆 Counting the closed contracts, his contract is still the one with the highest cumulative volume in the presidential book, USD 26.35M.
fracos: He stands at 20.50% in the winner contract, confirmed reading of 18/Oct, 17:44 BRT, and Flávio Bolsonaro's gap over him is 58.75pp.

He trails in eighteen of the twenty-one national polls conducted after the vote: 46% to 48% in Ipespe/Abrapel and 48.9% to 51.1% of the valid votes in Veritá of 17/Oct, 45% to 50% in Gerp, 45.9% to 46.8% in CNT/MDA and 47.5% to 49% in Futura/100% Cidades of 16/Oct, and 45% to 47% in Datafolha of 15/Oct.
He finished the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) 1.87 points behind Flávio Bolsonaro, with 45.16% of the valid votes against 47.03%.
In [Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) of 03/Oct government approval went from 46% to 44%, with 49% disapproval.
candidates.analise: Lula stands at 20.50% in the winner contract (cumulative volume USD 26.35M), confirmed reading of 18/Oct, 17:44 BRT, and falls 3.00pp against the confirmed reading of 17/Oct at 16:59 BRT, published in the previous update. 🗳️ He had 45.16% of the valid votes in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno). 📊 In Vox Brasil of 18/Oct he has 46.4% against 44.6%, after 44.2% to 42.7% on 09/Oct, and 51% of the valid votes; in Ipespe/Abrapel of 17/Oct he has 46% against 48% and in Gerp of 16/Oct 45% against 50%. On 17/Oct, Ipespe/Abrapel gave Flávio Bolsonaro 48% to 46% in total votes and Veritá 51.1% to 48.9% in valid votes, and Gerp, from the night of 16/Oct, gave 50% to 45%; on 16/Oct, CNT/MDA gave 46.8% to 45.9% and Futura/100% Cidades 49% to 47.5%, and PoderData/Aya measured 50% to 50% in valid votes. After the promulgation, Lula said the 6x1 work schedule will return if Flávio Bolsonaro wins the election (O Globo and Valor), and on 13/Oct he announced Prospera MEI, with forgiveness of individual microentrepreneurs' debts estimated at R$ 12.6 billion (Poder360 and Estadão). ⚖️ On 16/Oct the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) plenary unanimously approved, with André Mendonça as rapporteur, rules that link to the campaigns the WhatsApp and other platform channels that receive money, technical support or guidance from them, with mandatory registration (Gazeta do Povo and G1), and Justice Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva denied the Flávio Bolsonaro campaign's request to restrict the activity of unions and students on social media (CartaCapital, G1 and Estadão). On 15/Oct the court had unanimously struck down the 48-hour wait to reactivate channels registered after the deadline and ordered the removal of videos by the PL, Flávio Bolsonaro and Nikolas Ferreira that link Lula to the alleged [INSS](/en/glossary#inss) frauds (Folha de S.Paulo, Estadão and G1). In a statement on 16/Oct, Meta attributed to a gap in its safeguards the fact that its AI produced campaign material for Flávio Bolsonaro and not for Lula, said the problem had been fixed and denied interfering in the election (O Globo); on 17/Oct, the Flávio Bolsonaro campaign pressed Meta at the TSE and said it had also been harmed (Folha de S.Paulo). 🎙️ The first debate of the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), on Band, is scheduled for the night of 18/Oct, with a 30-minute free-confrontation segment, and Globo's for 23/Oct; Record cancelled the 11/Oct debate (Folha de S.Paulo, Band and Poder360). Lula gave an interview to Jornal Nacional on the night of 15/Oct and Flávio Bolsonaro on the night of 16/Oct, when he said he only needs one term (G1, Poder360 and UOL). For the afternoon of 18/Oct, before the debate, Flávio Bolsonaro had a rally scheduled on Avenida Paulista, and Lula's allies had rallies scheduled in major cities (VEJA and CartaCapital). ⛔ The panel does not attribute the price to the polls or to the campaign agenda: it measures the sides with each one's timestamp.

candidates.name: Flávio Bolsonaro
candidates.header: PRICE: 79.25% (cumulative volume USD 22.57M) in the winner contract, confirmed reading of 18/Oct, 17:44 BRT, rises 2.30pp against the confirmed reading of 17/Oct at 16:59 BRT, published in the previous update. BALLOT: 47.03% of the valid votes in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno). POLLS: ahead in eighteen of the twenty-one post-vote national polls, with 48% to 46% in Ipespe/Abrapel of 17/Oct and 50% to 45% in Gerp of 16/Oct; 44.6% to 46.4% in Vox Brasil of 18/Oct.
fortes: He finished the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) ahead, with 47.03% of the valid votes against Lula's 45.16%, in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally.
He stands at 79.25% in the winner contract, confirmed reading of 18/Oct, 17:44 BRT.

He leads eighteen of the twenty-one national polls conducted after the vote: 48% to 46% in Ipespe/Abrapel and 51.1% to 48.9% of the valid votes in Veritá of 17/Oct, 50% to 45% in Gerp, 46.8% to 45.9% in CNT/MDA and 49% to 47.5% in Futura/100% Cidades of 16/Oct, and 47% to 45% in Datafolha of 15/Oct.
He has the declared support of Podemos, Augusto Cury, Novo, ACM Neto, PP, União Brasil, Ronaldo Caiado, Romeu Zema and Michel Temer.
Among Ronaldo Caiado's voters, he has 56% against 15% in Ipespe, 54.9% against 26.9% in AtlasIntel and 57% against 19% in PoderData/Aya.
fracos: He trails in both Vox Brasil polls conducted after the vote, with 44.6% against 46.4% on 18/Oct and 42.7% against 44.2% on 09/Oct, and ties at 50% of the valid votes in PoderData/Aya of 16/Oct; between each pollster's previous and current wave, his lead in total votes falls from 5 to 2 points in Ipespe/Abrapel and from 9 to 5 in Gerp.

🏦 According to O Globo, the [Federal Police](/en/glossary#pf) is investigating, in the inquiry into Daniel Vorcaro and Master's relationship with BRB, the bank's R$ 3.1 million financing to Flávio Bolsonaro for the purchase of a R$ 6 million mansion in Brasília; he says the transaction was legal, and the report comes from a single media group and is included here with attribution.

📰 Messages extracted from Daniel Vorcaro's phone and published by Estadão on 24/Sep show four attempts by him to contact the banker between 13 and 16 November 2025, in the days before Vorcaro's arrest, on 17 November 2025. Gazeta do Povo confirmed the authenticity of the exchanges with its own sources close to the investigation.

Its fieldwork ended before the Band debate. candidates.name: Augusto Cury
candidates.header: ELIMINATED IN THE [FIRST ROUND](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno): third place, with 2.89% of the valid votes in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally. PRICE: winner contract closed and resolved at zero, with USD 5.51M cumulative. [SECOND ROUND](/en/glossary#segundo-turno): declared support for Flávio Bolsonaro on 08/Oct (G1, Estadão and CNN Brasil).
fortes: He finished third, with 2.89% of the valid votes, ahead of Renan Santos and Ronaldo Caiado.
The [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno)'s third-place book was resolved in his favour.
fracos: He is out of the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), and his contract in the winner book was resolved at zero.
On the eve the third-place book paid more for Renan Santos, 47.50%, and for Ronaldo Caiado, 30.00%, than for him, 23.70%.
candidates.analise: Augusto Cury finished the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) in third, with 2.89% of the valid votes in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally, and is out of the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno). His contract in the winner book was closed by Polymarket after the first round and resolved at zero, with USD 5.51M cumulative. The first round's third-place book, which on the eve paid 23.70% for him, at 23:00 UTC on 03/Oct, was resolved in his favour. 🤝 On 08/Oct he declared support for Flávio Bolsonaro in the second round (G1, Estadão and CNN Brasil).

candidates.name: Renan Santos
candidates.header: ELIMINATED IN THE [FIRST ROUND](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno): fourth place, with 2.24% of the valid votes in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally. PRICE: winner contract closed and resolved at zero, with USD 17.12M cumulative. [SECOND ROUND](/en/glossary#segundo-turno): he backs neither of the two.
fortes: He finished fourth, with 2.24% of the valid votes, ahead of Ronaldo Caiado, with 2.18%.
His contract in the winner book closed with USD 17.12M cumulative, the second largest in the presidential book.
fracos: He is out of the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), and his contract in the winner book was resolved at zero.
On the eve the third-place book paid 47.50% for him, and third place went to Augusto Cury.
candidates.analise: Renan Santos finished the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) in fourth, with 2.24% of the valid votes in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally, and is out of the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno). His contract in the winner book was closed by Polymarket after the first round and resolved at zero, with USD 17.12M cumulative, the second largest in the presidential book, behind Lula's. On the eve the third-place book paid 47.50% for him, at 23:00 UTC on 03/Oct, and it was resolved in favour of Augusto Cury. 🤝 On the night of 04/Oct he said he backs neither of the two in the second round and freed Missão's activists to choose (Gazeta do Povo and Agência Brasil).

candidates.name: Caiado / Haddad / Zema
candidates.header: ELIMINATED IN THE [FIRST ROUND](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno): Ronaldo Caiado, with 2.18% of the valid votes, and Romeu Zema, with 0.27%, in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally. Fernando Haddad did not run for President. PRICE: the three winner contracts were closed and resolved at zero.
candidates.subtitle: The three names outside the leading pack, with the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) final tally (100% of polling sections) and the closing of the winner contracts after the first round.

caiado.label: CAIADO (PSD), eliminated in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) with 2.18% of the valid votes in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally. His winner contract was closed and resolved at zero, with USD 7.82M cumulative.
caiado.fortes: He declared support for Flávio Bolsonaro in Goiânia on 06/Oct, with governor Daniel Vilela (O Globo and VEJA).
caiado.fracos: He finished fifth, behind Renan Santos, and the PSD decided on neutrality in the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) (Folha de S.Paulo and Agência Brasil).

haddad.label: HADDAD (PT), did not run for President: he ran for governor of São Paulo and lost to Tarcísio de Freitas in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno). His winner contract was closed and resolved at zero, with USD 7.74M cumulative.
haddad.fortes: The top of his series in the winner contract was 7.60%, on 26/May, measured in the database backup.
haddad.fracos: He was not measured by any national poll in a presidential scenario or in a second-round pairing.

zema.label: ZEMA (Novo), eliminated in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) with 0.27% of the valid votes in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally. His winner contract was closed and resolved at zero, with USD 7.74M cumulative.
zema.fortes: ⭐ In [Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) of 28/Sep, 81% of his voters would go to Flávio Bolsonaro in the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), the largest transfer among the names measured (O Globo).
zema.fracos: He had 0.27% of the valid votes. He declared his vote for Flávio Bolsonaro on 05/Oct, and Novo declared support for him on 07/Oct (G1 and CartaCapital).

candidates.analise: 🗳️ Ronaldo Caiado finished the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) in fifth, with 2.18% of the valid votes, and Romeu Zema had 0.27%, in the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) final tally. Fernando Haddad ran for governor of São Paulo, not for President. The three contracts in the winner book were closed by Polymarket and resolved at zero. 🤝 Romeu Zema declared his vote for Flávio Bolsonaro on the night of 05/Oct (G1 and Folha de S.Paulo), and Novo, his party, declared support on 07/Oct (G1 and CartaCapital). Ronaldo Caiado declared support for Flávio Bolsonaro in Goiânia on 06/Oct (O Globo and VEJA), even with the PSD neutral in the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) (Folha de S.Paulo and Agência Brasil).
fortes: Ronaldo Caiado declared support for Flávio Bolsonaro on 06/Oct (O Globo and VEJA), and Romeu Zema declared his vote for him on 05/Oct, followed by Novo on 07/Oct (G1 and CartaCapital).
⭐ In [Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) of 28/Sep, 81% of Romeu Zema's voters and 42% of Ronaldo Caiado's would go to Flávio Bolsonaro in the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) (O Globo).
fracos: The two are out of the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), and the winner contracts of all three names were resolved at zero.
Fernando Haddad did not run for President: he ran for governor of São Paulo and lost to Tarcísio de Freitas in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno).

Flávio Bolsonaro had said on 13/Oct that he would vote in favour, and he will attend the Band debate on 18/Oct after having said he would not (UOL, CartaCapital and CNN Brasil). ⚖️ On 16/Oct the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) plenary unanimously approved, with André Mendonça as rapporteur, rules that link to the campaigns the WhatsApp and other platform channels that receive money, technical support or guidance from them, with mandatory registration (Gazeta do Povo and G1), and Justice Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva denied the Flávio Bolsonaro campaign's request to restrict the activity of unions and students on social media (CartaCapital, G1 and Estadão). On 15/Oct the court had unanimously struck down the 48-hour wait to reactivate channels registered after the deadline and ordered the removal of videos by the PL, Flávio Bolsonaro and Nikolas Ferreira that link Lula to the alleged [INSS](/en/glossary#inss) frauds (Folha de S.Paulo, Estadão and G1). In a statement on 16/Oct, Meta attributed to a gap in its safeguards the fact that its AI produced campaign material for Flávio Bolsonaro and not for Lula, said the problem had been fixed and denied interfering in the election (O Globo); on 17/Oct, the Flávio Bolsonaro campaign pressed Meta at the TSE and said it had also been harmed (Folha de S.Paulo). 🎙️ The first debate of the second round, on Band, is scheduled for the night of 18/Oct, with a 30-minute free-confrontation segment, and Globo's for 23/Oct; Record cancelled the 11/Oct debate (Folha de S.Paulo, Band and Poder360). Lula gave an interview to Jornal Nacional on the night of 15/Oct and Flávio Bolsonaro on the night of 16/Oct, when he said he only needs one term (G1, Poder360 and UOL). For the afternoon of 18/Oct, before the debate, Flávio Bolsonaro had a rally scheduled on Avenida Paulista, and Lula's allies had rallies scheduled in major cities (VEJA and CartaCapital). 📊 The next national polls registered with the TSE come out on 18/Oct (Phoenix), 19/Oct (AtlasIntel, PoderData, BTG/Nexus, DataTrends and 100 Cidades), 20/Oct (Veritá and Alfa), 21/Oct ([Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest), Palver, Gerp, 100 Cidades and Ideia), 22/Oct (Datafolha, PoderData and Indexa) and 23/Oct (Vox Brasil, Ipespe, Veritá, DataTrends and Alfa). ⛔ The panel does not attribute price moves to the polls, the interviews, the endorsements or the day's acts: it measures the sides with each one's timestamps.
